sources.description: FIFA World Cup 2026 Team Prediction PDF pages 3 and 4: team creation, team page and invitecode requirements.
School JPA and MySQL guideline slides for repository, entity and service boundaries.
School MVC web-flow guideline slides for forms, DTO validation and controller flow.
School MVC and i18n guideline slides for Thymeleaf pages and resource bundles.
School security guidance carried by the PRD for user-only and owner-aware team flows.
Lesson notes for DTO validation, BindingResult and field error rendering.
Lesson notes for JPA repository and service-repository separation.
Project notes and school reminders carried into the team-management plan.
Exercise projects identified in the school reference map for JPA, validation and security patterns.
Existing call-the-match team model, membership model, invitecode behavior, team service and team screens.
Git repository for the call-the-match project.
User and project decisions carried into this plan: admin exclusion from teams and authenticated current-user lookup.

tasks.title: Scope Team Dashboard To Current User
tasks.description: Make the existing private team dashboard membership-aware before expanding team UI. Keep `/team/dashboard` on the MVC controller-to-service path, load persisted team rows for the authenticated normal user's memberships through the repository boundary, and stop the dashboard from rendering every team in the system.
acceptance_criteria: An authenticated USER can open `/team/dashboard` and receives team rows loaded through the team service from persisted memberships for the current user.
Dashboard team rows no longer include teams the current user has not joined or created.
Guest access stays blocked by the `/team/**` Spring Security boundary.
ADMIN remains excluded from team participation routes for this project.
Dashboard links continue into member-visible team routes without making private team data public.

tasks.title: Build Team Create Form Validation
tasks.description: Create the validated MVC form boundary for team creation on the dashboard. Use a request DTO with existing Jakarta Validation annotations, immediate BindingResult handling, Thymeleaf field errors and resource-bundle messages so later persistence work starts from school-style form input rather than writable entity binding.
acceptance_criteria: The private dashboard exposes a team create form backed by a request DTO rather than binding the Team entity directly.
Required create input uses existing Jakarta Validation annotations on the request DTO.
The create controller action uses `@Valid` with `BindingResult` immediately after the validated DTO and returns the form with field errors on invalid input.
Team create labels, validation messages and visible form feedback that belong in messages are backed by keys in `src/main/resources/i18n/messages.properties`.
The form boundary keeps team creation decisions in the service layer instead of the Thymeleaf view or controller.

tasks.title: Persist Created Team With Owner Membership
tasks.description: Complete the create-team vertical slice through service and repository persistence. Resolve the creator from the authenticated current-user boundary, keep team names and generated invitecodes unique, save the owner relation and owner TeamMember entry, and return the user to the private team flow with a usable new team.
acceptance_criteria: A valid create submission persists a Team through the service and repository layers for the authenticated current USER.
The created Team stores the authenticated user as owner without accepting a caller-provided owner id.
The creator receives an owner TeamMember relation so the created team appears on the private dashboard immediately.
Persisted team names remain unique and duplicate name attempts produce clear user-facing MVC feedback.
Invitecode generation yields a code of at least eight characters and checks generated uniqueness before the new team is accepted.
Guest and ADMIN actors cannot create participating teams through this flow.

tasks.title: Build Invite Code Join Form Validation
tasks.description: Make the invitecode join form a proper MVC input boundary before extending membership rules. Move raw invitecode input behind a request DTO, use Jakarta required-input validation with Thymeleaf field feedback, and prepare clear bundle-backed feedback for invalid join attempts on the dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: The dashboard invitecode join form posts through an MVC request DTO instead of relying on an unvalidated raw request field.
Required invitecode input uses existing Jakarta Validation annotations and invalid empty submissions render field feedback on the team dashboard.
The join controller action follows the school validation flow with `@Valid` and immediate `BindingResult` handling.
Join form labels and visible validation/error messages that belong in messages are backed by keys in `src/main/resources/i18n/messages.properties`.
This task prepares the input boundary without moving membership business rules into the controller or view.

tasks.title: Join Team From Authenticated Invite Code
tasks.description: Complete the invitecode join behavior through service and repository membership decisions. Resolve the join actor from authentication, find the target team by invitecode, save a single membership, reject invalid codes clearly, and prevent duplicate membership without reintroducing hardcoded user ids.
acceptance_criteria: A valid persisted invitecode joins the matched team for the authenticated current USER through the service and repository path.
The join flow never accepts or reconstructs the membership actor from a hardcoded or request-provided user id.
An unknown invitecode resolves to clear school-style MVC error or dashboard feedback rather than a raw framework page or silent failure.
Duplicate membership is blocked so the same user appears only once in a team.
Join success and failure feedback used by the screen is resource-bundle backed rather than hardcoded controller text.
Guest and ADMIN actors remain excluded from the invitecode join path.

tasks.title: Restrict Team Detail To Members
tasks.description: Turn the existing team detail view into a private member scoreboard slice. Keep `/team/{id}` behind member-aware service decisions before Thymeleaf receives team data, then render the owner, membership rows, personal scores and team total from persisted team data without exposing private score data to outsiders.
acceptance_criteria: A team member can open `/team/{id}` and receives team detail data through the controller-to-service boundary.
The detail view renders team name, owner and member rows backed by persisted Team and TeamMember data.
Member rows include personal score data intended for the private team page.
The team total uses the domain or service score source rather than score calculation in Thymeleaf.
A non-member cannot open another team's private page or receive its member score data through the MVC detail route.
Guest and ADMIN behavior stays explicit: guests are stopped at team-route security and admins are not admitted into team participation.

tasks.title: Protect Team Detail Error Paths
tasks.description: Close the error surface around private team detail browsing. Route missing teams and malformed team identifiers through the project's MVC exception and error-page direction while preserving the member-only privacy boundary for valid private data.
acceptance_criteria: A missing team id on the private detail path resolves through the chosen MVC not-found behavior.
An invalid team detail path variable resolves through school-style type mismatch MVC error handling instead of a raw framework page.
Shared MVC exception handling is reused for team detail error cases where it matches the project convention.
Error behavior does not expose private team membership or score data to non-members.
This task stays on MVC error handling and does not add REST error-response or WebClient work.

tasks.title: Make Invite Code Regeneration Owner-Only
tasks.description: Harden the existing invitecode regeneration action as an owner-only MVC mutation. Keep the visible control on the private team page for owners, require service-layer owner enforcement and CSRF-safe form behavior, regenerate a unique invitecode, and return bundle-backed feedback.
acceptance_criteria: A team owner can regenerate the invitecode from the private team screen through a CSRF-protected MVC mutation.
Invitecode regeneration is denied for non-owner members even when they forge a direct request.
The replacement invitecode remains unique before it becomes active.
Visible invitecode regeneration feedback comes from the resource bundle rather than hardcoded controller text.
The owner decision is enforced in service/repository behavior and not only by hiding a Thymeleaf control.

tasks.title: Add Owner Member Removal
tasks.description: Add the second owner management slice for team membership. Let owners remove members through a private MVC mutation that updates persisted membership data, hide management controls from non-owner members, and keep removal authorization outside the view.
acceptance_criteria: A team owner can remove a team member through an MVC action that updates persisted TeamMember data and returns to the private team page.
Non-owner members do not see member removal controls on the Thymeleaf team page.
Non-owner forged removal requests are blocked server-side.
Member removal decisions remain in the service and repository boundary instead of controller or Thymeleaf business logic.
Guest and ADMIN actors remain outside owner team-management actions.

tasks.title: Add Team MVC And Security Closure Tests
tasks.description: Close the visible team flows with school-required MVC and security evidence after dashboard, create, join, detail and owner routes are stable. Cover model/view/redirect/error behavior and the actor matrix for guest, normal user, admin, member and owner without adding REST or e2e scope.
acceptance_criteria: MVC controller tests verify the dashboard is current-user scoped and renders persisted team data through the expected model contract.
MVC tests cover observable create, join and private detail behavior using status, view, model, binding, redirect or error assertions.
Security tests verify guest denial from team routes and normal USER access to allowed team flows.
Security tests verify ADMIN exclusion from team participation for this project.
Security tests verify non-member team detail denial and non-owner denial for owner-only mutations.
This task does not add REST controller, WebClient or e2e tests to team management.

tasks.title: Add Team Validation And Membership Rule Tests
tasks.description: Add focused late evidence for team DTO validation and membership rules that are clearer below the MVC surface. Use the school validation test category for existing Jakarta annotations and service-focused tests or equivalent focused verification for create/join and uniqueness-sensitive membership decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Validation tests using a Jakarta Validator cover existing annotation behavior for team create DTO required input.
Validation tests using a Jakarta Validator cover existing annotation behavior for invitecode join DTO required input.
Focused service tests or equivalent focused evidence cover owner membership creation when a team is created.
Focused service tests or equivalent focused evidence cover duplicate join prevention and invalid invitecode handling.
Uniqueness-sensitive team name or invitecode rules introduced by this feature have focused verification at the boundary that owns them.
The validation and membership rule tests do not broaden into REST controller, WebClient or unrelated scoring recalculation work.
